messages.subject: Update: Upcoming 0.7.0 Release
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
Just an FYI that are a number of exciting things in the pipeline. I'm planning a first proper release with 0.7.0 and will be asking for help in testing release candidates towards the end of January. Most of this development is taking place at https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/refactor-packages but I will be switching the google code repo over to git and keeping it in sync with github sometime this month.

The goals for the 0.7.0 release all revolve around packages:

1) The existing package management code that we've been borrowing from the r-project.org <http://r-project.org> will be replaced by a more flexible system built on the maven repository model and will be compatible with maven, ivy, gradle/sbt/etc, jenkins, and other pillars of the jvm ecosystem. This will allow:

a) R(enjin) packages will be assembled as JARs with the namespace and serialized R code as resources
b) Any JAR in a maven-compatible repository can be loaded through the library() or require() function, if an artifact doesn't have a specific R namespace definition, all public classes defined in the artifact will be loaded into the search path
c) Renjin will have a pluggable package resolution mechanism. That is, during deployment, renjin might only be configured to load packages from the classpath, whereas in interactive mode renjin will fetch the packages from a local and remote repositories
d) R language packages can be built for renjin using either
   i) maven plugin that allows the developer to seamlessly mix R and Java/Scala/etc code
   ii) simple command line that builds based on a DESCRIPTION file or from an existing source archive

2) We are setting up build server that will continuously test and build existing CRAN packages and deploy them to a maven repository. This should make it trivial to reference existing R packages from either a java/scala project or from the interactive repl

3) To make sure as many as possible of the CRAN packages work, I am focusing on completing and testing the S4 class system and gcc-bridge, which compiles existing C and fortran code to JVM byte code.

Best,
Alex
